newsitem.title: COMOROS: New prime minister named in Comoro Islands.
newsitem.headline: New prime minister named in Comoro Islands.

text.p: President Mohamed Taki of the Comoro Islands appointed Ahmed Abdou as his prime minister on Friday, three weeks after general elections in the tiny Indian Ocean archipelago.
Ahmed Abdou, 60, is a veteran administrator who has been finance minister several times. Public finances are in a catastrophic state with most civil servants unpaid for the past 11 months.
Taki named his new prime minister a day after he returned from official visits to China, Singapore and Mauritius.
In a separate decree on Friday Taki instructed the senior civil servants in ministries to assume control until new ministers are appointed.
Ahmed Abdou takes over from Tajiddine Ben Said Massonde who remained in office with his ministers on a caretaker basis after the early December elections boycotted by the opposition.
Taki's ruling party, the National Rally for Development, won 36 of the 43 seats in the federal assembly. Independents won four and the Islamist party three.
The opposition boycotted the polls because it feared rigging.
